description: You are a Security Engineer responsible for improving Linux host monitoring coverage. The Linux audit subsystem (auditd) generates detailed security event logs at /var/log/audit/audit.log on monitored endpoints, but Wazuh currently has no decoder pipeline for these logs — privilege escalation attempts, credential file access, and suspicious syscalls are passing through entirely undetected. Your goal is to build a complete auditd monitoring and detection framework. The end state must include: (1) a custom decoder chain — at minimum a parent decoder and a child decoder — in Wazuh's decoder configuration that can parse Linux audit.log format and extract relevant fields such as syscall type, process name, and file path; (2) at least two custom detection rules triggered by auditd events, covering at minimum two distinct threat categories (for example: privilege escalation via setuid/setgid syscalls, unauthorized access to /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd, or suspicious process execution via execve); (3) at least one of those rules must include a MITRE ATT&CK technique mapping using the <mitre> element; (4) a CDB lookup list in /var/ossec/etc/lists/ containing at least 3 high-risk executable paths (e.g. /usr/bin/sudo, /bin/su, /usr/bin/pkexec) for rule enrichment; and (5) ossec.conf updated to actively monitor the audit log location on endpoints. A sample audit.log file has been staged at /var/log/audit/audit.log inside the Wazuh manager container for testing. Log in to the Wazuh dashboard at https://localhost with username admin, password SecretPassword.
